card.name: Undead Immunities
card.effect: Undead Immunities. Tags: lich, undead. You are immune to poison damage, the Poisoned condition, disease, Frightened, Charmed and magical sleep. You no longer need to breathe. You still require the normal rest schedule for mechanical recovery and can still be affected by abilities that specifically target undead unless another feature says otherwise.

source.originalText: Undead Immunities: Become immune to poison, disease, fear, sleep, and mind control.

card.effect: You may change Beast appearance to another stored source as a Bonus Action without resummoning or restoring HP. It gains either+10 ft swim or climb Speed until it ends. No new release, attack or capture.

card.name: Serum Tolerance
card.effect: Serum Tolerance. Negative side effects printed on serum profiles do not affect you. Strain generation and Strain penalties still apply normally. This does not suppress drawbacks printed on mutation cards, Hero transformations or Mutation Overload.

source.originalText: Serum Tolerance: You can consume serums without the normal toxicity effects that would affect others.

card.name: Intimidating Transformation
card.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies of your choice within 20 feet that can see you
card.effect: Intimidating Transformation. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn and then repeats the save. On a failure by 10 or more, it would instead be Stunned until the end of its next turn, subject to the Warrior hard-control guard. A target succeeding on the initial save is immune to this use. The transformation does not force surrender or belief changes.

source.originalText: Intimidating Transformation: Undergo a particularly terrifying mutation that can cause enemies to become frightened or even paralyzed with fear.

card.name: Controlled Transformation
card.effect: Controlled Transformation. You can suppress obvious cosmetic signs of dormant mutations and reduce visible manifestations of active mutations enough to pass as merely scarred or unusually built while fully clothed. You gain advantage on checks to conceal your Warrior mutations from casual visual inspection. This never suppresses mechanical mutation effects, defeats magical detection or conceals transformations whose cards explicitly make you Large, monstrous or otherwise impossible to hide.

source.originalText: Controlled Transformation: Your mutations appear less monstrous and can be partially concealed when necessary.

card.name: Warding Mutation
card.rangeAndTarget: Self; protects one ally within 10 feet at a time
card.effect: Warding Mutation. Grow temporary protective plates for 3 rounds. At the start of each of your turns choose one ally within 10 feet. Until the start of your next turn, the first time that ally takes damage reduce it by S+M, minimum 0. The prevented damage is simply negated rather than transferred. This is a temporary transformation, not an equipped mutation, and cannot stack with itself.

source.originalText: Warding Mutation: Develop protective growths that can absorb damage directed at allies.

card.name: Adaptive Perfection
card.effect: Final Form – Adaptive Perfection. Choose up to three damage types from acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant or thunder that have actually damaged you since your last long rest, plus one environmental hazard you personally experienced during that period. For 3 rounds you are immune to the chosen damage types and ignore ordinary penalties from the chosen hazard. You cannot choose a type or hazard you did not actually encounter, and multiple immunity sources do not stack.

source.originalText: Final Form – Adaptive Perfection: For 3 rounds, gain immunity to the damage types and environmental effects you've been exposed to during the current day.

card.name: Adaptive Mutation
card.effect: Adaptive Mutation. Trigger when you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison or another Director-approved environmental damage type, or when an environmental hazard forces you to make a saving throw. Gain resistance to that damage type or advantage on saves against that specific hazard for 3 rounds. Choose one if both apply. This is a temporary transformation and consumes no mutation slot or serum.

source.originalText: Adaptive Mutation: Rapidly evolve your body to counter a specific threat or environmental hazard.

card.name: Abomination Ascendant
card.effect: Final Form – Abomination Ascendant. For 3 rounds your melee reach increases by 5 feet, your Speed increases by 10 feet and you gain a natural Claw attack dealing 2d8 + M slashing damage. At the start of each enemy's turn within 30 feet that can see you, it makes a Wisdom save; on failure it is Frightened until the end of that turn. The hard-control guard still applies to any other denial effect you use. This transformation grants no free attacks or additional Actions.

source.originalText: Final Form – Abomination Ascendant: Transform into a nightmarish creature for 3 rounds, gaining terrifying new attacks and abilities while causing fear in a 30-foot radius.

card.name: Consumed
card.effect: LIMITATIONS: your body increasingly displays your Mystery and imposes -2 on checks made specifically to disguise or conceal those supernatural alterations without magical assistance. Significant body changes require armor and fitted gear to be refitted during ordinary downtime at the Director's normal maintenance cost; this never destroys attuned equipment. value.name: Consumed
value.blurb: Your Mystery remakes your body until its element shows through
limitations: As you gain levels, your appearance shifts toward your Mystery's theme: flame hair, starlit eyes, bone protrusions, and the like
Some civilized NPCs react with fear or awe; concealing the change in formal courts requires ongoing effort
As your body changes, armor and gear must be refitted periodically (roleplay / downtime cost)

boons.name: Curse Boon I
boons.description: Gain +5% resistance aligned with your Mystery's element or theme (fire, necrotic, force, psychic, etc.). Once per day, suppress visible transformation for 1 hour in civilized areas — the Mystery still leaks through divination.

boons.name: Curse Boon II
boons.description: Elemental skin: +1 AC while wearing light or no armor as your flesh hardens into mystery-matter. Unarmed strikes and natural weapons you wield count as magical and deal +1d4 thematic damage.

boons.name: Curse Boon III
boons.description: Mystery infusion: weapon and touch attacks deal +1d4 thematic damage matching your Mystery. Revelation potency visibly bleeds into your strikes.

boons.name: Curse Boon IV
boons.description: Partial transformation: ignore difficult terrain tied to your Mystery (fire walks, shadow steps, temporal stutter, etc.). Allies who follow within 1 tile during the same round may treat that terrain as normal ground until your next turn.

boons.name: Curse Boon V
boons.description: Once per day, fully embody your Mystery's element for 3 rounds — immunity to that damage type, +2 effective Revelation potency, and visible manifestation (aura, wings of flame, star corona, etc.). Allies within 2 tiles gain +1 AC as your transformation steadies the battlefield; suppression is impossible while the embodiment lasts.

card.name: Spirit Walk
card.acquisition: choose first at Oracle 6; a distinct second at Oracle 13
card.effect: Your spirit leaves your body until the end of the turn. During the effect you may move through creatures and nonmagical solid barriers, ignore difficult terrain and cannot be targeted by attacks or effects that require a physical target. You may activate one other known Revelation at its normal RC cost while in spirit form. You cannot manipulate physical objects or make weapon attacks. At turn end choose your original space or a legal unoccupied space you reached; if none is legal, return to the original space. Your physical body remains in its original space and can still be attacked normally; damage and conditions on either form affect your one character. The optional Revelation uses its normal activation and cost: this feature grants no free Action. Ending in an occupied or illegal space returns the spirit to its body.

v6Records.text:
Temporary Hit Points

A buffer against damage, lost before normal HP. Cannot be healed. Do not stack (take the higher value if you gain more). Do not restore consciousness at 0 HP. Last until depleted or after a long rest, unless specified otherwise.

Consume Decay. When you are adjacent to a corpse or significant amount of decaying organic matter, you can use your action to absorb nutrients from it. You gain temporary hit points equal to your level that last for 1 hour. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Battle Cry. As a bonus action, you can let out a mighty battle cry. Each ally within 30 feet of you who can hear you gains temporary hit points equal to your level. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Soul Drain. As an action, you can touch one creature and draw out a portion of its life essence. The target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). On a failed save, the creature takes necrotic damage equal to 1d6 + your Intelligence modifier, and you gain temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt. This damage increases to 2d6 at 6th level, 3d6 at 11th level, and 4d6 at 16th level. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

coreSupports.text:
1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.

druidMetadata.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Entering Shapeshift clears the Refrain counter because the Druid changes the body sounding the Weave; beast-form casting remains limited by class features.
workedExample: Druid 5 Moon, WIS 16 PB 3 S 2 M 3: RP 12, shifts 3, Buffer Reserve 13, Form Surges 3, HP 30/38. Prepare 8 ranked spells plus three cantrips.

Turn 1 Bonus Action Bear: shifts 3→2, draw 13 of requested 20 buffer, reserve 13→0, temp HP 13. Action claw attack PB+WIS=+6, damage 2d6+3+1 plus Moon first-hit 2. Shifting clears the Refrain counter and remembered repeated-spell name; accumulated Dissonance is unchanged.
Enemy deals 10 damage: temp HP 13→3, real HP 30 remains. No additional beast HP exists.
Turn 2 Moon healing Bonus Action spends 2 RP, RP 12→10, rolls 2d8=7, HP 30→37. It cannot repair the buffer reserve. Action claw as usual.
Turn 3 Bonus Action change Wolf spends another shift, shifts 2→1. Old Bear temporary HP ends. Wolf bite 1d8+3, target STR against DC 14 or Prone. No new buffer, RP or Form Surge generated.
At 10 this character gains Moon Hero forms; Arch forms still wait until 11. At 20 unlimited changes still cannot refill Buffer or Surge reserves.
